parsed.title: The domination-number conjecture for total graphs of finite rings
parsed.statement:
Let $R$ be an arbitrary ring with Jacobson radical $J$, and suppose that

$$
R/J=M_{n_1}(F_1) \times \ldots \times M_{n_k}(F_k),
$$

where each $F_i$ is a finite field and $n_i\geq 2$ for all $i$. For a finite ring $A$, let $\tau(A)$ denote its total graph and let $\gamma(\tau(A))$ denote the domination number of that graph. **Domination-number conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(\tau(R))=\min_i\{n_i(|F_i|-1)+1\}.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the corresponding upper bound without the restrictions $n_i\geq 2$. The examples of $M_2(\mathbb{Z}_2)$ and $M_3(\mathbb{Z}_2)$ attain this bound, while factors with $n_i=1$ can give a strictly smaller domination number; the equality in the stated generality is therefore proposed but not established here.
parsed.source_name: David Dolžan and Polona Oblak, “The total graphs of finite rings”, arXiv:1401.1941 (2014).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.1941

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

parsed.title: Left Gog–GOGAm trapezoid equienumeration conjecture
parsed.statement: For $k\leqslant n$, a left Gog or GOGAm trapezoid of shape $(n,k)$ is obtained from the corresponding triangle by retaining the $k$ leftmost diagonals. **Left Gog–GOGAm trapezoid conjecture.** For all $k\leqslant n$, the $(n,k)$ left Gog and GOGAm trapezoids are equienumerated. The paper gives a bijective proof for trapezoids with one or two diagonals, while the general case is posed as the conjectural extension.
parsed.source_name: Philippe Biane and Hayat Cheballah, “Inversions and the Gog-Magog problem”, arXiv:1401.6516 (2014).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

parsed.title: Non-periodicity conjecture for rows of the three-pile Sharing Nim nim-value table
parsed.statement:
Let the rows of Table 1 consist of the nim-values $\mathcal{G}(0,a,n)$ as $n$ varies, with the corresponding fixed row parameter $a$.

**Non-periodicity conjecture.** Rows of Table 1 are not ultimately periodic.

The bottom row and the main diagonal are shown to be not ultimately periodic, while the analogous assertion for all rows is presented as a conjecture motivated by this phenomenon and by the dependence of a row on lower rows.
parsed.source_name: Nhan Bao Ho, “Three-pile Sharing Nim and the quadratic time winning strategy”, arXiv:1506.06961 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

parsed.title: The hypertree F-positivity conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypertree, and let $X_H$ denote its chromatic symmetric function. The $F$-basis is the fundamental quasisymmetric-function basis. **Hypertree F-positivity conjecture.** For every hypertree $H$, $X_H$ is $F$-positive. This would follow from finding the required partition of the nonconstant colorings for every edge size; the result is established when all edge sizes are prime, and also for edge size $4$, but remains open in general.
parsed.source_name: Jair Taylor, “Chromatic Symmetric Functions of Hypertrees”, arXiv:1506.08262 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08262

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

parsed.title: Schur-positivity conjecture for linear interval hypergraphs
parsed.statement: Let $H$ be a hypergraph with chromatic symmetric function $X_H$. An **interval hypergraph** is a hypergraph isomorphic to one with vertex set $[n]$ in which every edge has the form $i,i+1,ots,j$. It is **linear** if $|e\cap e'|\leq 1$ for every pair of distinct edges $e,e'$. **Linear interval hypergraph conjecture.** If $H$ is a linear interval hypergraph, then $X_H$ is Schur-positive. The paper presents this as a modest hypergraph analogue of Stanley's clawfree graph conjecture; no proof or resolution is supplied, so the conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Jair Taylor, “Chromatic Symmetric Functions of Hypertrees”, arXiv:1506.08262 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08262

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

parsed.title: The bounded-expansion characterization via poset dimension
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of graphs closed under taking subgraphs. For each integer $h\geq 1$, consider posets of height $h$ whose cover graphs belong to $\mathcal{C}$.

**Bounded-expansion characterization.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded expansion if and only if, for each $h\geq 1$, the posets of height $h$ whose cover graphs are in $\mathcal{C}$ have bounded dimension.

The theorem proved in the paper establishes one of the two implications; the converse remains open. Thus the conjecture proposes a characterization of bounded-expansion graph classes in terms of uniformly bounded dimension for bounded-height posets with cover graphs in the class.
parsed.source_name: Gwenaël Joret, Piotr Micek and Veit Wiechert, “Sparsity and dimension”, arXiv:1507.01120 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.01120

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2015). “Note that Theorem shows one of the two directions of this conjecture, the other one remains open.”

parsed.title: Coefficientwise domination conjecture for even-rank partition-poset homology
parsed.statement:
Let $\alpha_{2n}$ be the Frobenius characteristic of the representation on maximal chains of $\Pi_{2n}$, and let $R_{2n}$ be the Frobenius characteristic of the homology of the even-rank subposet $\Pi_{2n}^e$. Write $a_i(2n)$ and $b_i(n)$ for the coefficients of $h_2^i h_1^{2n-2i}$ in $\alpha_{2n}$ and $R_{2n}$, respectively.

**Coefficientwise domination conjecture.** The symmetric function $\alpha_{2n}-R_{2n}$ is a nonnegative integer combination of homogeneous symmetric functions $h_\lambda$ indexed by partitions $\lambda$ of $n$ whose parts are $1$ or $2$. Equivalently,

$$
b_i(n)\leq a_i(2n)\qquad\text{for all }2\leq i\leq n.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening suggested by the available data; the source gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Sheila Sundaram, “Some Problems Arising from Partition Poset Homology”, arXiv:1507.02365 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02365

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

parsed.title: Ryjáček's conjecture on locally connected graphs
parsed.statement:
A finite, simple, undirected graph $G$ is **locally connected** if, for every vertex $u$ of $G$, the subgraph induced by the neighborhood $N_G(u)$ is connected. It is **weakly pancyclic** if it has a cycle of every order $\ell$ between its girth $g(G)$ and circumference $c(G)$.

**Ryjáček's conjecture.** Every locally connected graph is weakly pancyclic.

This conjecture proposes that local connectivity forces a graph to contain cycles of all orders between its shortest and longest cycle. The source states it as motivation for the paper; no resolution is supplied here.
parsed.source_name: Christoph Brause, Dieter Rautenbach and Ingo Schiermeyer, “Local Connectivity, Local Degree Conditions, some Forbidden Induced Subgraphs, and Cycle Extendability”, arXiv:1507.07486 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.07486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

parsed.title: Haiman's Schur–P positivity conjecture for fixed-point-free involution Stanley symmetric functions
parsed.statement: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group and let $\mathcal{I}(S_n)$ denote its involutions. For a fixed-point-free involution $y\in\mathcal{I}(S_n)$, let $\hat F^{\operatorname{FPF}}_y$ be its fixed-point-free involution Stanley symmetric function. **Schur–$P$ positivity conjecture.** For every fixed-point-free $y\in\mathcal{I}(S_n)$, the symmetric function $\hat F^{\operatorname{FPF}}_y$ is Schur–$P$ positive. This predicts a positive expansion in the Schur–$P$ basis for the fixed-point-free analogue of involution Stanley symmetric functions; the source presents it as an open conjecture following known positivity results in related cases.
parsed.source_name: Zachary Hamaker, Eric Marberg and Brendan Pawlowski, “Involution words: counting problems and connections to Schubert calculus for symmetric orbit closures”, arXiv:1508.01823 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01823

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

parsed.title: Stanley–Hibi–Li conjecture for marked chain and order polytopes
parsed.statement:
Let $(P,A,\mathbf{\lambda})$ be a marked poset. For an $N$-dimensional polytope $Q$, let $f_i(Q)$ denote the number of its $i$-dimensional faces, and write $\mathcal{C}_{P,A}(\mathbf{\lambda})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{P,A}(\mathbf{\lambda})$ for the marked chain and marked order polytopes. **Stanley–Hibi–Li conjecture.** For all $i=0,1,\ldots,|P\setminus A|$,

$$
f_i(\mathcal{C}_{P,A}(\mathbf{\lambda}))\geq f_i(\mathcal{O}_{P,A}(\mathbf{\lambda})).
$$

The original conjecture concerned unmarked chain and order polytopes; the facet case is known for marked chain and marked order polytopes, while the zero-dimensional marked case remains open, and the full marked statement is therefore unresolved.
parsed.source_name: Xin Fang and Ghislain Fourier, “Marked chain-order polytopes”, arXiv:1508.02232 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02232

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

parsed.title: GCD representatives for compressed zero-divisor graph classes in quotients of UFDs
parsed.statement:
Let $D$ be a unique factorization domain and let $I$ be an ideal expressed as a minimal union of principal ideals

$$
I=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\langle n_\alpha\rangle.
$$

Let $\"]\phi:D\to D/I$ be the canonical homomorphism, and let $\"][x]$ denote the annihilator-equivalence class of a nonzero zero-divisor $x$ in the compressed zero-divisor graph.

**GCD-representative conjecture.** For every $a\in D$,

$$
[\phi(a)]=\left[\phi\left(\gcd\{a,n_\alpha\mid\alpha\in\Lambda\}\right)\right].
$$

This would provide canonical gcd-type representatives for compressed zero-divisor graph classes in quotients by ideals with minimal principal-union expressions.
parsed.source_name: Rachael Alvir, “Zero-Divisor Graphs of Quotient Rings”, arXiv:1508.02432 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

parsed.title: Ratio conjecture for independent sets in regular graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, and let $H_{d,n}$ denote the disjoint union of $n/(2d)$ copies of $K_{d,d}$, assuming that $2d$ divides $n$. For each $k$, let $i_k(G)$ be the number of independent sets of size $k$ in $G$. **Independent-set ratio conjecture.** For all $k$, the ratio

$$
\frac{i_k(G)}{i_{k-1}(G)}
$$

is maximized by $H_{d,n}$. The source presents this as a stronger conjecture than the extremal conjecture for the individual coefficients; its resolution is not given.
parsed.source_name: Ewan Davies, Matthew Jenssen, Will Perkins and Barnaby Roberts, “Independent Sets, Matchings, and Occupancy Fractions”, arXiv:1508.04675 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.04675

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

parsed.title: The Short Cycle Cover Conjecture for bridgeless graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph with $m$ edges, and let the **length of a cycle cover** be the sum of the lengths of all cycles in the cover. **Short Cycle Cover Conjecture.** Every bridgeless graph with $m$ edges has a cycle cover of length at most $1.4m$.

This conjecture, attributed in the paper to Alon and Tarsi, concerns quantitative bounds on the shortest cycle cover. The paper proves upper bounds for bridgeless cubic graphs, but does not resolve the stated bound for all bridgeless graphs.
parsed.source_name: Barbora Candráková and Robert Lukoťka, “Short cycle covers on cubic graphs using chosen 2-factor”, arXiv:1509.07430 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07430

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

parsed.title: Site recurrence for non-backtracking coalescing random walk on bounded degree trees
parsed.statement: A **non-backtracking coalescing random walk** is a coalescing random walk in which each particle moves to a neighboring vertex other than the vertex from which it most recently arrived; particles may coalesce according to any priority scheme. A tree has **bounded degree** if its vertex degrees are uniformly bounded. Site recurrence means that the specified site is visited by particles infinitely often. **Site recurrence conjecture.** Non-backtracking coalescing random walk with any priority scheme is site recurrent on bounded degree trees. The conjecture extends the established site recurrence result for the priority scheme that remembers paths of particles moving toward the root, and remains open for other priority schemes.
parsed.source_name: Itai Benjamini, Eric Foxall, Ori Gurel-Gurevich, Matthew Junge and Harry Kesten, “Site recurrence for coalescing random walk”, arXiv:1510.04721 (2015).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.04721

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

parsed.title: Rank conjecture for the lifted inclusion matrices of arcs
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ be a finite field with characteristic $p$, let $G\subset\mathbb{F}_{q}^{k}$ be an arc, and let $M_{G}^{\uparrow n}$ denote the matrix defined in the paper from the $(2k-3+n)$-element arc $G$ and its $(k-1)$-subsets. Let the condition in the cited corollary mean that, for every arc $G\subset\mathbb{F}_{q}^{k}$ of size $2k-3+n$, the matrix $M_{G}^{\uparrow n}$ has full row rank. **Rank conjecture.** If $0\leq n\leq q$ and

$$
2\leq k\leq\min\left\{p+n(p-2),\frac{q+4-n}{2}\right\},
$$

then this condition holds; equivalently, every arc $G\subset\mathbb{F}_{q}^{k}$ of size $2k-3+n$ has $M_{G}^{\uparrow n}$ of full row rank. This conjecture would provide a broad rank criterion for proving the $q+1$ upper bound in the MDS conjecture.
parsed.source_name: Ameera Chowdhury, “Inclusion Matrices and the MDS Conjecture”, arXiv:1511.03623 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03623

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

parsed.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the normal rational curve
parsed.statement: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ be a finite field with characteristic $p$. For an arc $G\subset\mathbb{F}_{q}^{k}$ of size $2k$, let $H_{G}^{\uparrow 2}$ be the matrix defined in the paper, and let $v\in\mathbb{F}_{q}^{\binom{2k}{k-1}}$ be the vector whose first $k$ coordinates are $1$ and whose remaining coordinates are $0$. **Normal rational curve uniqueness conjecture.** If $k\leq2p-2\leq q$, then for every arc $G\subset\mathbb{F}_{q}^{k}$ of size $2k$, the column space of $H_{G}^{\uparrow 2}$ contains $v$. If true, this would imply that the normal rational curve is the unique arc of size $q+1$ up to linear equivalence in the stated range. The claim is supported by computational evidence, while the general classification problem remains open.
parsed.source_name: Ameera Chowdhury, “Inclusion Matrices and the MDS Conjecture”, arXiv:1511.03623 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03623

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

parsed.title: Jonckheere–Lou–Bonahon–Baryshnikov conjecture on highest demand vertices
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a large but finite graph with negative curvature. Let the **demand** of a vertex mean the quantity measuring how many shortest paths pass through it, as defined in the paper. **Jonckheere–Lou–Bonahon–Baryshnikov's highest-demand conjecture.** There are very few vertices with the highest demand. The paper discusses counterexamples and limitations of this formulation, including graphs with uniformly distributed or infinite demand.
parsed.source_name: Matthew Yancey, “Negatively Curved Graphs”, arXiv:1512.01281 (2021).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01281

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2015). “Dourisboure and Gavoille prove that $k$-disk-tree terminates when $k$ is at least three times the tree-length of the graph, giving a bound that equals the result from layering trees.”

parsed.title: The linear-components conjecture for perfect codes containing Preparata codes
parsed.statement:
Let $C$ be a binary perfect code containing a Preparata code, and let an $i$-component denote the corresponding component of $C$. The set $\{(x,x,|x|)\}$ is the model linear component, where $|x|$ denotes the parity of $x$.

**Linear-components conjecture.** Every $i$-component of $C$, for every $i$, is linear; equivalently, it is equivalent to

$$
\{(x,x,|x|)\}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the structure of components in perfect codes containing Preparata codes. The paper gives no proof or resolution of the assertion.
parsed.source_name: Denis S. Krotov and Anastasia Yu. Vasil'eva, “On perfect codes that do not contain Preparata-like codes”, arXiv:1512.03048 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03048

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

parsed.title: Korpelainen et al.'s conjecture on finite definition and labelled well-quasi-ordering
parsed.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a hereditary graph class, meaning that it is closed under taking induced subgraphs, and suppose that $\mathcal{C}$ is well-quasi-ordered under the induced subgraph relation. The class is **labelled well-quasi-ordered** if, for every well-quasi-order of labels, its labelled graphs contain no infinite antichain under the labelled induced subgraph relation. **Korpelainen et al.'s conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ is finitely defined if and only if it is labelled well-quasi-ordered. Every labelled well-quasi-ordered class is already known to be finitely defined, so the open part is the converse for well-quasi-ordered hereditary classes.
parsed.source_name: Aistis Atminas and Robert Brignall, “Well-quasi-ordering and finite distinguishing number”, arXiv:1512.05993 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05993

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2015). “This conjecture remains open (and is still widely believed), but it was shown recently that the corresponding question for unlabelled well-quasi-ordering is false.”

parsed.title: Equality of Krull-dimension bounds for Khovanov-Rozansky homology
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph and let $E$ be a subset of its edge set $E(G)$. Write $\mathscr{H}_0^\mathbb{Q}(G)$ for the degree-zero Khovanov-Rozansky homology over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathscr{H}_0(G)$ for the corresponding homology over $\mathbb{Z}$. For a module over a ring, write $\mathrm{K}\text{-}\dim$ for its Krull dimension. **Krull-dimension equality conjecture.** For every such $G$ and $E$, 
$$
\mathrm{K}\text{-}\dim_{\mathbb{Q}[E]} \mathscr{H}_0^\mathbb{Q}(G)=\mathrm{K}\text{-}\dim_{\mathbb{Z}[E]} \mathscr{H}_0(G)-1.
$$
 The conjecture asserts that the inequality proved in the surrounding discussion is always an equality; establishing this would rule out the possibility that rational coefficients yield a strictly stronger upper bound for the graph invariant $\alpha_E(G)$.
parsed.source_name: Hao Wu, “Khovanov-Rozansky homology and Directed Cycles”, arXiv:1508.07337 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.07337

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).
